title: Set the practice metronome to 100 for the next piece and start it ticking
instruction: The metronome is still at 160 from the last piece. Set it to 100 for the next piece and start it ticking on its own.
context: Learning an instrument is common: two thirds of US adults (66%) have learned to play one at some point (YouGov, 2022), and the metronome is its standard practice aid, "often recommended to music students without reservation" (Wikipedia, Metronome). The clockwork pyramid (Maelzel's design, 1815) is set the only way it can be: slide the weight on the rod to the tempo, swing the rod and let it tick. It was wound when practice began; between pieces only the tempo changes. The hard parts, in order. (1) Hold the case down while the other hand drags the weight up: its spring clip grips the rod with about 3 N, more than the 171 g metronome weighs (1.68 N), so pulled one-handed the whole metronome lifts and the weight stays put. (2) Stop it within 1.5 mm of the 100 mark after a 22.7 mm drag: 96 and 104 sit 1.5 mm either side. (3) Swing the rod past 15 degrees and take both hands clear while the light case stays standing.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. (1) Metronome: a Wittner Taktell Piccolo 836, black (series 830; a clockwork pyramid metronome, tempo 40 to 208; about US$45 to 80 from music retailers; 155 mm tall, base 70 x 45 mm, 171 g per retailer listings), its spring wound, standing loose on the bare table, its base centred on (255, 0), its front (pendulum and tempo scale) facing the right arm (-y), its back toward the left arm; its winding key, on its +x side, is not used. Case: a black stepped pyramid, 70 mm wide (along x) and 45 mm deep at the base up to 60 mm, 58 x 39 mm up to 110 mm, 44 x 31 mm up to its top at 155 mm. Pendulum: a 3 x 1.5 mm steel rod, 7 mm in front of the lower front face, on a pivot 55 mm up, its tip 150 mm up; its counterweight (a 22 mm disc, 12 mm thick, 16 mm below the pivot) hangs inside the case. Sliding weight: a block 20 mm front to back (16 mm proud of the rod's front), 16 mm across, 14 mm tall, 5 g, a red pointer line on its top front edge; its spring clip holds it on the rod until it is pushed or pulled along the rod with about 3 N. Rod and counterweight 44 g, case 122 g. Scale: a white strip on the case's front behind the rod, a dark mark at every Maelzel tempo from 40 (top) to 208 (bottom), each level with the weight's pointer when the weight is set to it, long marks at 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 144, 160 and 208. The weight's centre sits 43.7 mm over the pivot at 160 and 66.4 mm at 100; 96 and 104 are 1.5 mm either side of 100. Start: the weight's pointer level with the 160 mark, the pendulum hanging still and upright. Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial. Checks before the first trial (spring scale 0 to 10 N, kitchen scale, ruler, phone stopwatch); use the metronome only if all pass: total mass 150 to 200 g; with the case held down, the weight starts to slide along the rod at 2 to 4 N, and pulled up with the case not held, the case lifts off the table; set to 100 and started, 8 ticks span 4.0 to 4.4 s (7 intervals) and it ticks 48 to 52 times in 30 s; set to 160, 78 to 82 times in 30 s.
scoring: Sim reads the metronome's pose, its pendulum's angle, the weight's place on the rod and both grippers at every 0.05 s step; the real trial reads a 30 fps trial video with its sound, an end photo and a ruler. The same windows and tolerances apply to both. Tick: the pendulum passing upright (sim: its angle changing sign between two steps, the time interpolated; real: each audible tick, timed on the video's sound track). Timed: the last 8 ticks before the end, with no two of them 1.6 s or more apart and the last one under 1.6 s before the end; every swing between two of them reaching 15 degrees or more each side (real: the rod's tip 25 mm or more either side of upright on the video); both grippers' finger zones 30 mm or more from every part of the metronome on every step from just before the first of them to the end (real: no finger within 30 mm over that stretch of video, a 30 mm block between each hand and the metronome in the end pose); and the case standing on the table over the same stretch: tilted under 10 degrees, its underside within 3 mm of the table (real: video against the table line). Where the case stands does not matter. Tempo: 60 divided by the mean interval of those 8 ticks (7 intervals), in beats per minute (real: the time from the first to the eighth tick on the sound track, divided by 7). Set: the weight's pointer (its top front edge) within 2.5 mm of the 100 mark, along the rod (sim: the weight's place on the rod; real: calipers or a ruler on the end photo, pointer to mark). Score, at the last step: 1.0 if timed at 96 to 104 per minute; 0.75 if timed at 90 to 110; 0.5 if not, but the weight set; 0.25 if timed at any other tempo with the weight not set; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0; every end state falls in exactly one. The score never reads the order of moves or which hand did what: pulled up with the case not held, the weight does not slide but lifts the whole metronome, so it stays at 160; a pendulum kept going by hand, or held up off the table, is not timed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The case is loose on the table (friction 0.45 to 0.5); the rod and counterweight swing on an undamped hinge, the weight on a slider. One rule, the clip: a 4000 N/m spring whose anchor holds under 3 N along the rod and follows the weight at 3 N. No escapement or mainspring: the rod swings at its own rate. The inner layout, masses and friction are design values (not published) set to beat on the scale; the setup's checks test the mass, the clip and the tick rates.
reset_notes: Stop the pendulum and let it hang upright. Hold the case down and slide the weight back down until its pointer is on the 160 mark. Wind the key fully. Stand the metronome back on its tape marks, base centred on (255, 0) mm, its front toward the right arm. Nothing is consumed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (one arm idle: 0.0 left idle, 0.0 right idle)
